From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: we do not accept the Seller's framing

- **"[STANDARD]" labels, the "FINAL" marking and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note".** These are counterparty assertions. Nothing in our own authority process confirms that any position was "settled at principal level", "cleared by both sides" or "agreed" (playbook §0.4 / §6.3). Every clause below is therefore reviewed in full, whatever its label.
- **"Market standard" preamble.** This is advocacy, not a source of authority. We assess each term against our playbook, not against the Seller's description of the market.
- **Inconsistency between the Seller's own documents.** The Seller Update presents several points (Bluefen, Riverlark, the incident, title) as resolved. The Disclosure Letter confirms they are not (DL §§2, 3, 6, 10). DL §11 also says expressly that no position or approval is included. We should rely on the Disclosure Letter facts, not the Update's characterisations.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, i.e. AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), labelled [STANDARD].
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, i.e. AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft. No such authority has been given, and the figure matching our fallback does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter on the playbook terms.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. The Seller also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion for general claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insist on 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The default wording is a hidden override that would sweep Title, Tax, fraud and indemnity claims into the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to the existence of what we are buying. A 20% cap on a 100% share purchase is not an administrative matter.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express carve-out. This point is non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** Under the playbook no one may waive this position, and the Seller's "any nature" wording would purport to cap the Seller's own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL §§1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete DL §§1.1–1.2 and accept only specific disclosures that are fairly identified.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would effectively empty the warranties. We have not "already accepted" this framework, whatever the Seller's note says.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier should rely on named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete cl 8.3.
- **Reason:** Combined with SPA-N-006, it would bar claims on every disclosed risk, including Bluefen, Ironquay and DD-006.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both as Conditions Precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make an effective consent plus satisfied conditions a hard CP.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). DL §2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that conditions are satisfied, so the Update's "addressed" is not accurate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payout letter, direct repayment in the funds flow, and releases at Completion.
- **Reason:** DL §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which we have.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, shown as a specific line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a specific funds-flow line, or an explicit Seller-funded mechanism, covering on-costs.
- **Reason:** Leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow means the Company, and so the Buyer, would bear them. DL §5 is also silent on on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment, and described as "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened IP indemnity covering ownership, the transfer of Project Materials and confirmatory assignment, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Broaden the indemnity and require a confirmatory assignment or evidence of payment.
- **Reason:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes the transfer of Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. No receipt or assignment exists (DL §4). The AUD 180,000 figure in DD-010 is unverified either way, so we should not fix the indemnity to that number.

**SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular updates before and after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Add covenants on preservation, investigation and updates, with appropriate protection.
- **Reason:** DL §6 confirms that access, scope and notification duty are all undetermined for about 1,240 records. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction, and we should not concede immateriality either.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual (DD-008 read with DD-011).
- **Recommendation:** Reserve the position. Request information and do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet.
- **Reason:** DL §8 does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We should neither concede ordinary course nor automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single general regime applied to "all Claims", including Title, Tax and IP (cl 12.3 / 13 / 12.8; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime").
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment, indemnity and covenant categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Draft express separate regimes and delete the catch-all language.
- **Reason:** Several clauses work together to collapse every category into the 20% / 18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (for example an ASIC search, a PPSR search, constitution and board approvals, and an encumbrance confirmation).
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept. Require independent verification as a CP or Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. DL §10 itself says the Buyer has not verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP to remain OPEN, to be negotiated separately.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep both OPEN.
- **Reason:** No agreement is confirmed through our authority process. We should not assume either unlimited liability or that the point has been resolved.

---

## Other points noted (not escalated)
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The disclosures describe a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not a consent to the share sale. We should confirm this on our own reading of the documents rather than relying on the Seller's summary.
- **DL §1.4 (non-admission).** Acceptable in principle, provided it is not used to undercut specific disclosures or the CPs above.

## Escalation to Amelia Frost
No fallback has been authorised, so the mark-up should go back on starting positions throughout. If the deal team wants to use the 20% cap or the 18-month fallback, or accept a post-Completion Riverlark release, each needs Amelia Frost's prior written approval for this specific draft.
